To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ti substitution in the wurtzite ZnO lattice results in a large distortion, and the sample grown in a mixed ambient of 80%Ar and 20%O2 exhibits the largest magnetic moment.
Ti-doped ZnOS thin films grown in a mixture ambient of 80%Ar and 20%O2 exhibit the largest saturation magnetization.

the electronic and chemical states of Ti ions in Ti-doped Zn O thin films are highly dependent on the ambient conditions during growth, and that a mixture of 20% O 2 and 80% Ar is optimal for obtaining a large magnetic moment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of ambient atmosphere on the electronic and chemical structures of Ti-doped ZnOs.
the electronic and magnetic properties of Ti doped ZnO films grown under different conditions.
the electronic and chemical states of Ti ions in ZnO thin films.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ti substitution in ZnO is the origin of magnetism, and that the magnetism is enhanced by the presence of a large number of Ti-O-Ti bonds.
Ti doping in ZnO thin films can be used as a magnetic material with the magnetic moment depending on the ambient conditions.
the ambient conditions play a key role on the Ti speciation, local structure, and magnetic properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ambient condition plays a critical role in the growth of Zn1-xTixO thin films, and the Ti substitution in ZnO lattice is the key to induce magnetic properties.
the Ti substitution is the main factor that induces the magnetic moment, and the local structures of the Ti ions are also critical for the magnetic properties of ZnO.
the magnetic moment is strongly dependent on the Ti coordination and the Ti valence state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetic properties are closely related to the chemical and structural environment of the Ti ions.
the magnetic properties of Ti-doped ZnOs are closely linked to the local structures and the valence state of Ti ions.
the magnetic properties can be tuned by controlling the ambient atmosphere during film growth.
